info.title: Trinary Exchange API
info.description:
Public API for Trinary Exchange - the market data and enrichment layer for the EVE Frontier economy.

This API exposes four data domains:

- **Trading data**: order books, trades, price history, and market activity across Trinary Exchange trade hubs.
- **Keyspace enrichment**: decoded and contextualized on-chain state from the EVE Frontier world contracts.
- **Organization data**: Armature organizations, including governance structure, treasuries, and organizational units.
- **Frontier enrichment**: general reference data for EVE Frontier entities such as items, systems, and structures.

All requests are served through an authenticated gateway. Authenticate with the `x-api-key` header. Each operation's `x-cu-cost` is the Compute-Unit charge deducted per call.

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

The job board: open agreements by default, newest first. Filter by status, currency, minimum reward, source or destination hub, cargo or wanted items, lister, hauler and whether a claim gate applies; pass `claimable_by` to learn whether an address can accept each one. Fillers who hold the wanted items search accepted jobs by `want_collection_id`/`want_asset_id`. Each side of the haul names its trade hub and whether its collection is a known warehouse vault. Paged with a self-contained `cursor` (it carries the filters). `lapsed` and `overdue` are derived from wall-clock time, which the response returns as `evaluated_at`; events still reach the index with its delay (see `X-Indexer-Checkpoint`).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return (1–100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response’s `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Comma-separated statuses (default `open`): `open`, `lapsed`, `accepted`, `overdue`, `delivered`, `defaulted`, `forfeited`, `cancelled`, `closed_lapsed`. Ignored on a `cursor` request: the cursor carries the original filters.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Only agreements paid in this coin type.

parameters.name: min_reward
parameters.description: Only agreements whose reward is at least this, in the smallest unit of their currency (u64 decimal). Combine with `currency`.

parameters.name: source_hub_id
parameters.description: Only cargo picked up at this trade hub.

parameters.name: destination_hub_id
parameters.description: Only deliveries handed in at this trade hub.

parameters.name: cargo_collection_id
parameters.description: Only cargo of this warehouse-receipt collection.

parameters.name: want_collection_id
parameters.description: Only agreements that want items of this collection delivered (for fillers who already hold them).

parameters.name: cargo_asset_id
parameters.description: Only cargo of this item type ID.

parameters.name: want_asset_id
parameters.description: Only agreements that want this item type ID delivered.

parameters.name: lister
parameters.description: Only agreements posted by this address.

parameters.name: hauler
parameters.description: Only agreements accepted by this address.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Only agreements posted on behalf of this organization by a trusted wrapper. No wrapper is trusted yet, so this matches nothing.

parameters.name: gated
parameters.description: `true`: only agreements with a claim gate (limited to listed players, machine keys or organizations); `false`: only agreements anyone can accept.

parameters.name: claimable_by
parameters.description: Add `eligibility` to each row: whether this address can accept it.

parameters.name: accept_deadline_before
parameters.description: Only agreements whose accept deadline is before this time (Unix epoch milliseconds). With `status=lapsed`, the listings lapsed long enough for the config admin to close.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order (default `posted_desc`, newest first). `reward_desc` compares raw amounts, so filter by `currency` with it. Ties break on `agreement_id`.

parameters.name: min_checkpoint
parameters.description: Serve data that includes at least this indexer checkpoint (e.g. the checkpoint of your transaction). A cached copy older than this is rebuilt. Every response carries `X-Indexer-Checkpoint`: the checkpoint it includes. If the indexer has not reached this checkpoint yet, the response waits briefly, then returns current data with a lower checkpoint header — retry later.

The consolidated coin list, enumerated from the token registry so coins with no triex pool (e.g. CRED) still appear. Each coin merges registry identity, on-chain supply/contract facts (circulating supply is total minus known treasury holdings), and market data appended from the indexer's coin pools (null when the coin has no pool). get.description:
**Cost:** 150 compute units per request.

Live open orders across trade hub markets, ordered by last activity (newest first). Orders on hubs that no longer exist are excluded. Each row carries the hub display name (`hub_name`) and power state (`hub_state`, online/offline), so callers need not resolve them separately. All filters compose freely: scope by trade hubs (`storage_unit_ids`), by item (`asset_id`), by owner (`trading_account_id`), and by side. Private-shared hubs are resolved by the caller — pass the hub list you can see; omit it for all hubs, or set `public_only=true` to restrict to location-revealed (public) hubs, or `include_public=true` to widen `storage_unit_ids` to also cover every public hub. Set `exclude_offline=true` to drop orders on offline hubs. Pagination is a single self-contained `cursor` param: pass `next_cursor` to page backward or `prev_cursor` to poll for new activity. Cursors embed the original filters, so no other params are needed (and filters are ignored) on cursor requests.

parameters.name: storage_unit_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated trade hub IDs and/or item collection IDs (max 100). Omit for all trade hubs.

parameters.name: asset_id
parameters.description: Numeric item type / asset id. Omit for all items.

parameters.name: trading_account_id
parameters.description: Only orders owned by this trading account ("my orders").

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: Filter by order side (default: both). `buy` = bids.

parameters.name: public_only
parameters.description: Set `true` to restrict to location-revealed (public) assemblies. Omit for all visible hubs.

parameters.name: include_public
parameters.description: Set `true` to return orders on the `storage_unit_ids` hubs OR on any location-revealed (public) hub. Without `storage_unit_ids` it behaves like `public_only=true`.

parameters.name: exclude_offline
parameters.description: Set `true` to drop orders on hubs that are offline (`hub_state` `offline`). Hubs with no known state are kept. Omit to include them.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response (`next_cursor` for the next page, `prev_cursor` to poll for new activity). Self-contained: it carries the original filters and limit, so other params are ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page (default and max 100).

get.summary: Unified open-orders discovery feed across trade hubs

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

Plain market display prices (no trading fee applied) from the `display_price` view; a client that wants to show a fee applies the viewer's own rate for the pool. Pass `item_ids` alone for vault-independent item-tier prices (one per item). Pass `item_ids` + `storage_unit_ids` to run the full traded → item → book → unknown waterfall per (item, vault); a pair with no pool falls back to the vault-independent item-tier price (`tier: "item"` with a null `pool_id`) unless `fallback=false`, and comes back `tier: "unknown"` when the item has no price anywhere. `storage_unit_ids` may hold either trade hub ids or vault item collection ids.

parameters.name: item_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated numeric item (asset) IDs. Batch ceiling: at most 100 IDs per request — larger batches are rejected with 400.

parameters.name: storage_unit_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated trade hub / vault item collection ids. When present, must match the number of `item_ids` (paired by position) or be a single id (applied to every item).

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.description: Pair mode only. Set to "false" to disable the item-tier price fallback for pairs with no pool at the requested vault (default: enabled). Ignored in item-only mode.

400.description: Missing/non-numeric `item_ids`, more than 100 IDs, or mismatched `storage_unit_ids` length.

get.summary: Batch display prices for items (optionally per vault)

get.description:
**Cost:** 20 compute units per request.

Convenience single-item form of `/display-prices`. With `storage_unit_id`, returns the per-vault waterfall price; without it, the vault-independent item-tier price.

parameters.name: item_id
parameters.description: Numeric item (asset) id

parameters.name: storage_unit_id
parameters.description: Trade hub / vault item collection id to price against.

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.description: Pair mode only. Set to "false" to disable the item-tier price fallback when no pool exists at the vault (default: enabled). Ignored without `storage_unit_id`.

get.summary: Display price for a single item (optionally at a vault)

get.description:
**Cost:** 30 compute units per request.

Returns the raw record of a single fill event, with no account perspective applied: both maker and taker fees and trading accounts are included. `asset_id` and `storage_unit_id` are `null` until the market’s metadata has been indexed. Responds 404 if the event digest is unknown.

parameters.name: event_digest
parameters.description: Fill event identifier: the transaction digest with the event index appended.

404.description: No fill with this event digest exists.

get.description:

Returns aggregated fee reserve (fees deposited minus fees withdrawn) and total open-order liquidity depth across all markets at each hub. Amounts are raw integers encoded as strings. Hubs that no longer exist are omitted from the result. Results are cached for 30 seconds. Maximum 200 IDs per request.

parameters.name: ids

Returns the item types (`asset_id`) that currently have open orders at the given trade hub, with flags indicating whether buy orders (bids) and/or sell orders (asks) exist. The full set is always returned in a single page — `next_cursor` is always `null`. Results are cached for 30 seconds.

parameters.name: hub_id

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

Returns the live order book for one item at a trade hub in a single request: resting bids and asks (bids highest-price-first, asks lowest-price-first), plus the resolved pool_id and pool metadata (asset names, decimals, taker fee) needed to price, size, and place orders against the book. Pass quote_type to prefer a market quoted in a specific currency. Responds 404 when the hub has no trading vault. When the hub trades but no market exists for this item yet, responds 200 with pool_id null and an empty book.

parameters.name: hub_id
parameters.description: Trade hub (storage unit) object ID

parameters.name: asset_id
parameters.description: Numeric item type ID

parameters.name: quote_type
parameters.description: Quote asset type string; exact matches are preferred.

parameters.name: hub_id

Returns the item collection (`collection_id`) backing the hub and the hub vault's configuration object (`vault_config_id`).

parameters.name: hub_id
parameters.description: Sui object ID of the trade hub

parameters.name: min_checkpoint
parameters.description: Serve data that includes at least this indexer checkpoint (e.g. the checkpoint of your transaction). A cached copy older than this is rebuilt. get.summary: Get vault configuration for a trade hub

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

Authoritative current contents per storage, straight from the chain indexer — the spendable truth that overlay containers merely arrange. The whole read is scoped by `storage_unit_id`; the item collection is derived from it server-side. One call can read several storages at once: pass `owner_address` for the wallet warehouse, `trading_account_id` for marketplace (trading account) holdings, `vault_ids` for organization (DAO) receipt vaults, and/or `inventory_key` for the trade hub hangar (keyed by game `type_id`, not collection-scoped). Sections whose selector was not passed come back empty. All amounts are raw integers as decimal strings.

parameters.name: storage_unit_id
parameters.description: Trade hub scoping the whole read. The item collection is derived from it server-side (each hub backs exactly one collection), so no collection id is passed. A hub with no known collection fails with `404 not_found`.

parameters.name: owner_address
parameters.description: Holder wallet — returns warehouse balances.

parameters.name: trading_account_id
parameters.description: Trading account — returns marketplace balances.

parameters.name: vault_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated organization (DAO) receipt vault ids — returns per-vault balances.

parameters.name: inventory_key
parameters.description: Inventory field key (hub or character `owner_cap_id`) selecting which hangar — when passed, returns hangar contents (by type_id).

404.description: No item collection is known for `storage_unit_id` (`not_found`).

get.summary: Get authoritative inventory balances at a trade hub

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

Returns the location of every located hub with a live sell order for the given item (type_id), newest location first. Hubs without a reported location are not listed. Paginated: pass back `next_cursor` as `cursor` to fetch the next page.

parameters.name: item_id
parameters.description: The type_id of the tradeable item to filter by

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return (1–100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response’s `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page.

get.summary: List locations that have a specific item for sale

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

Same as `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}` but accepts up to 200 IDs at once via the `ids` query parameter. Returns one entry per requested ID, in request order; IDs that do not resolve return an entry with null fields and `metadata.error_reason = "unresolved"`. Results are cached per organization for 5 minutes.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated organization object IDs (max 200).

parameters.name: min_checkpoint
parameters.description: Serve data that includes at least this indexer checkpoint (e.g. the checkpoint of your transaction). A cached copy older than this is rebuilt. Every response carries `X-Indexer-Checkpoint`: the checkpoint it includes. If the indexer has not reached this checkpoint yet, the response waits briefly, then returns current data with a lower checkpoint header — retry later.

400.description: `ids` is missing, empty, or has more than 200 entries.

get.summary: Batch-get organizations by ID

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

Returns top-level organizations (never their internal units) for a "discover organizations" listing. Each entry carries a member count as a size hint plus an icon and description when the organization has configured them. Sorted by member count (largest first) by default; pass `sort=name` for alphabetical. Paginate with `limit` and the returned `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of organizations to return (1–50).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response’s `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order: `members` (member count, largest first — the default) or `name` (alphabetical).

get.summary: List organizations for the discovery directory

get.description:
**Cost:** 30 compute units per request.

Resolves an organization object ID to the full organization: name, metadata, treasury and related object IDs, current members, and the complete tree of child units (`ous`). The ID may be the top-level organization or any unit within its tree — the top-level organization is always returned. Results are cached for up to 5 minutes, dropped as soon as the indexer reports a change.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Object ID of the organization — the root organization or any unit within its tree.

parameters.name: min_checkpoint
parameters.description: Serve data that includes at least this indexer checkpoint (e.g. the checkpoint of your transaction). A cached copy older than this is rebuilt. Every response carries `X-Indexer-Checkpoint`: the checkpoint it includes. If the indexer has not reached this checkpoint yet, the response waits briefly, then returns current data with a lower checkpoint header — retry later.

404.description: No organization exists with the given ID.

get.summary: Get an organization and its full unit tree

get.description:
**Cost:** 30 compute units per request.

Agreements related to the organization (OU), newest first: `gated_to` (default) lists those its board members may claim, `claimed_via` those accepted through it, `posted_for` those posted on its behalf by a trusted wrapper (none is trusted yet). Only this exact OU counts: the chain checks its board, not its sub-units’. `lapsed` and `overdue` are derived from wall-clock time, which the response returns as `evaluated_at`; events still reach the index with its delay (see `X-Indexer-Checkpoint`).

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Object ID of the organization (OU).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return (1–100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response’s `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: relation
parameters.description: How the agreements relate to the organization (default `gated_to`): `gated_to` = its board members may claim them; `claimed_via` = they were accepted through it; `posted_for` = posted on its behalf by a trusted wrapper (none is trusted yet, so this is empty). Ignored on a `cursor` request: the cursor carries the original filters.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Comma-separated statuses (default: all). Ignored on a `cursor` request: the cursor carries the original filters.

parameters.name: min_checkpoint
parameters.description: Serve data that includes at least this indexer checkpoint (e.g. the checkpoint of your transaction). A cached copy older than this is rebuilt. Every response carries `X-Indexer-Checkpoint`: the checkpoint it includes. If the indexer has not reached this checkpoint yet, the response waits briefly, then returns current data with a lower checkpoint header — retry later.

get.summary: An organization’s hauling agreements

get.description:
**Cost:** 30 compute units per request.

Returns every governance proposal of the organization, newest first: identity, creation time, lifecycle status, vote tallies, the off-chain metadata IPFS CID, the governance config the proposal was created under (still available after the on-chain proposal is deleted on execution or expiry), and — for composite proposals — the ordered step list. Snapshot weights are not included; read those from the live on-chain object while the proposal exists.

parameters.name: org_id
parameters.description: Object ID of the organization.

get.summary: List an organization's proposals

get.description:
**Cost:** 30 compute units per request.

Returns every keyspace the address can reach: keyspaces registered by one of the player’s organizations (`created`), keyspaces granted directly to the address as a player (`player_grant`) or machine key (`machine_grant`), and keyspaces granted to one of the player’s organizations (`ou_grant`). The player’s organizations are resolved automatically, so only the address is required. Results are read live on every call — never cached — so a freshly granted keyspace shows up as soon as the indexer has it.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Player wallet address.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Optional role filter (`grant`, `read`, or `write`). Narrows the grant-based matches; keyspaces the player’s organizations created are always included.

400.description: address param is missing, or role is not one of grant/read/write.

get.summary: List the keyspaces a player can access

get.description:
**Cost:** 50 compute units per request.

Agreements the address plays a part in, newest first: as `lister`, `cap_holder`, `beneficiary`, `hauler`, or `claimed_via_org` (accepted through an organization whose board it sits on). Each row lists the roles in `viewer_roles`. Filter with `role` and `status`. `lapsed` and `overdue` are derived from wall-clock time, which the response returns as `evaluated_at`; events still reach the index with its delay (see `X-Indexer-Checkpoint`).

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Player wallet address.

get.summary: Calculate a route between two solar systems
get.description:
**Cost:** 100 compute units per request.

Runs an A* search over the stargate network plus every jump-drive hop within
`max_jump_range_ly`, and returns the ordered waypoints together with the
route's jump counts and travel distance.

**Choosing an optimization.** `time` minimises travel time and will take long
jump-drive hops to skip gate chains. `fuel` minimises fuel burn and prefers
stargates, which are free but slower. `balanced` interpolates between them
using `gate_weight`.

**Ship parameters matter.** `mass` scales fuel burn per light year, so a
heavier ship shifts `fuel` and `balanced` results toward gates;
`max_jump_range_ly` bounds which drive hops exist at all, so a short-range
ship may be routed entirely over gates — or get a 404 when no gate path
exists.

**Reading the result.** `total_cost.total_jumps` is the hop count a player
sees; `gate_jumps` and `drive_jumps` split it by hop type;
`total_distance_ly` is the whole path and `drive_distance_ly` only the
jump-drive portion. A 404 means either that a name has not been reported
by any player yet (the message says which), or that the systems are known
but unreachable under these parameters — retrying with a larger
`max_jump_range_ly` may succeed. Waypoints through systems whose name has
not been reported carry a `null` `solar_system_name`.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Solar system name to depart from (case-insensitive).

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: Solar system name to arrive at (case-insensitive).

parameters.name: optimization
parameters.description: Which cost to minimise: `fuel`, `time`, or `balanced` (default `time`).

parameters.name: mass
parameters.description:
Ship mass, in the game's mass units. Heavier ships burn more fuel per
light year, so raising this pushes `fuel` and `balanced` routes toward
stargates (default 1.0).

parameters.name: gate_weight
parameters.description:
How much to favour stargates over jump drives, 0.0–1.0, used only by
`balanced` (default 0.5). 0.0 behaves like `time`, 1.0 like `fuel`.

parameters.name: max_jump_range_ly
parameters.description:
Ship's maximum jump-drive range in light years (default 50.0). Jumps
longer than this are excluded from the graph before the search runs.

200.description: The optimal route under the given parameters

404.description: Unknown solar system, or no route between them

Field semantics match the Trinary Exchange market-data API (`ErrorResponse`)
so a client can share one error handler across both services.

error.description:
Machine-readable error code (snake_case). Stable across releases — branch
on this field, never on `message`. Codes: `invalid_request`,
`unauthorized`, `not_found`, `internal`.

message.description:
Human-readable explanation of the failure. Wording may change at any
time; do not parse.

source.description: `recipe`: a digital chemistry recipe (cycle 7 on; nearly all crafting). `industry`: a legacy industry blueprint (a few remain, none runnable). `construct`: a construction-site structure.

primaryTypeId.description: The item the blueprint is keyed by: its main output for `manufacture`/`construct`, the ore or salvage consumed for `refine`.

kind.description: `manufacture`: build an item from parts. `refine`: refine or reprocess ore, crude matter or salvage, often into several outputs. `construct`: a construction-site structure (null `blueprintId`, no facilities). `reverse`: the backward half of a production loop (unpacking, D2 Fuel → Salt); do not price items from these.

runTime.description: Run time in seconds (raw game-client value); -1 when unknown.

outputs.description: Items produced per run. More than one for most `refine` blueprints and a few `manufacture` ones.

facilities.description: Facilities that can run the blueprint. Empty for `construct` entries, and for the few industry blueprints no facility can run.

typeId.description: Item type id of the facility (e.g. a Refinery or Printer).

maxInputRuns.description: Maximum input runs per job in this facility. Industry blueprints only.

maxOutputRuns.description: Maximum output runs per job in this facility. Industry blueprints only.

maxMultiplier.description: Maximum job multiplier in this facility. Digital chemistry recipes only.

BlueprintItem.description: One input or output line of a blueprint. For a digital chemistry recipe it is a slot: an input can name a type, require traits, or both.

id.description: Item type id (joins to the item list `id`). Null for a trait-only input slot, which any stack meeting `traits` fills; see `candidates`. Outputs always have an id.

name.description: Display name; for a trait-only slot, its trait names. May be empty.

quantity.description: Units consumed or produced per run. Fractional for continuous-quantity items (see the item list's `quantityKind`). For an output with `yield`, the nominal amount.

slot.description: Input or output index within the recipe (`recipe` entries only).

traits.description: Traits (named property ranges) the stack in this input slot must meet.

candidates.description: Trait-only slots: neotypes whose natural property ranges could meet `traits`. `guaranteed` means every variant of the type does; otherwise only some variants.

traitsGuaranteed.description: Typed slots with `traits`: whether every variant of the type meets them.

yield.description: Outputs whose amount varies: `breakpointTable` means it scales with an input property (`yieldPropertyId`), e.g. ore quality.

A point in the star map, in meters from the galactic origin.

Coordinates are decimal strings, not JSON numbers: the values exceed 2^53
and would lose precision in any IEEE-754 double (including every JavaScript
client). The same representation is used by the market-data API's hub
locations.

trades.description: Number of trades in this quote currency.

computed_at.description: When these aggregates were computed. Results are cached for up to 60 seconds. Unix epoch milliseconds.

trades_daily_30d.description: Daily trade counts over the last 30 days, oldest first.

new_pilots_daily_30d.description: Daily new-pilot counts over the last 30 days, oldest first.

orgs_with_vaults.description: Distinct organizations with at least one active vault.

hubs_with_storage.description: Trade hubs with shared storage enabled.

pilots_with_access.description: Distinct pilots with access to a shared vault (direct grants plus organization-derived grants, deduplicated).

volume_raw.description: Traded volume in raw quote units (integer, decimal string).

volume.description: Traded volume in human-readable quote units.

quote_symbol.description: Ticker symbol of the quote currency the volume is in.

member_count.description: Members across the organization’s line units.

h24.description: Trades executed in the last 24 hours.

d7.description: Trades executed in the last 7 days.

all_time.description: Distinct accounts that have ever traded.

d7.description: Distinct accounts that traded in the last 7 days.

trading_account_id.description: Trading account object ID the snapshot is for.

as_of_checkpoint.description: Checkpoint sequence number up to which this snapshot is current, or `null` if freshness could not be determined. Data typically lags the chain by a few seconds.

pools.description: Pools where the account has settled (claimable) or owed balances.

items.description: Idle item balances already held by the trading account.

coin_pools.description: Coin pools where the account has settled (claimable) or owed balances, or fee-tier turnover still to fold.

base_asset_id.description: Base coin type of the pool — the first type argument to use when withdrawing settled amounts.

quote_asset_id.description: Quote coin type of the pool — the second type argument to use when withdrawing settled amounts.

settled.description: Settled amounts, claimable into the trading account.

owed.description: Amounts currently owed by the account (informational).

open_order_count.description: Number of orders the account still has open on this pool.

pending_turnover.description: Maker-fee turnover this pool holds for the account, not yet folded into its exchange-wide fee-tier turnover (raw quote units, decimal string). Non-zero means `pool::fold_pending_turnover` would raise the account's turnover.

pending_turnover_epoch.description: Epoch of the newest pending entry; null when none.

collection_id.description: Object ID of the item collection.

amount.description: Item amount held (raw integer, decimal string).

storage_unit_id.description: Storage unit (trade hub) object ID backing the collection, or `null` if not yet indexed.

vault_config_id.description: Object ID of the hub's vault configuration, or `null` if not yet indexed.

collection_id.description: Object ID of the pool's item collection.

asset_id.description: Item type (asset) ID traded by the pool.

quote_asset_id.description: Quote coin type of the pool — the type argument to use when withdrawing settled amounts.

storage_unit_id.description: Storage unit (trade hub) object ID backing the market.

vault_config_id.description: Object ID of the hub's vault configuration.

settled.description: Settled amounts, claimable into the trading account.

owed.description: Amounts currently owed by the account (informational).

open_order_count.description: Number of orders the account still has open on this pool.

pending_turnover.description: Maker-fee turnover this pool holds for the account, not yet folded into its exchange-wide fee-tier turnover (raw quote units, decimal string). Non-zero means `multicoin_pool::fold_pending_turnover` would raise the account's turnover.

pending_turnover_epoch.description: Epoch of the newest pending entry; null when none.

trading_account_id.description: Trading account object ID on this side.

kind.description: `player` for a wallet-owned trading account, `org` for one held by an organization's trading custody; `null` when the account's owner is not indexed.

id.description: The player's wallet address, or the organization's object ID. `null` when unresolved.

name.description: The player's current character name, or the organization's name. `null` when unknown.

root_org_id.description: Organizations only: object ID of the top-level organization this one sits under (itself when it is the top level). `null` for players.

root_org_name.description: Organizations only: name of the top-level organization. `null` for players or when unknown.

owner.description: `player:<wallet_address>` for a character-owned trading account, or `ou:<org_id>` for an organization-owned one; null if unresolved.

owner_name.description: Matching character or organization's display name, or null.

root_ou_id.description: Top-level organization ID when the owner is a sub-organization; else null.

tribe_url.description: URL of the tribe's public page.

Waypoint.description: A waypoint in a calculated route

distance_ly.description:
Length of the hop that reaches this waypoint, in light years. Present
only for `jump_drive` hops — stargate hops have no traversal distance.

jump_type.description:
How this waypoint is reached from the previous one. `start` on the first
waypoint, then `stargate` or `jump_drive` per hop.

solar_system_id.description: Numeric solar system ID of this hop.

solar_system_name.description: Human-readable solar system name, or `null` when unavailable.
